Title: AADK backs mandatory drug screening for all Malaysia Airlines pilots, cabin crew
Article:
JERTIH, Aug 8 — The National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) supports the move by Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) to make it compulsory for 1,260 Malaysia Airlines (MAS) pilots to undergo drug screening following the recent arrest of one of its pilots in Indonesia.
AADK director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the move to tighten security controls and extend mandatory drug screening to all active pilots and cabin crew members was in line with the zero-tolerance policy towards drug abuse and trafficking.
“Safety in the aviation sector cannot be compromised because this industry bears a great responsibility for the lives of thousands of passengers,” he said after officiating the AADK’s Madani Foster Village (KAM) and Madani Foster School (SAM) programmes at Felda Tenang here today.
He said the AADK is ready to cooperate with MAG through drug abuse detection operations, strengthening the Drug-Free Workplace (TEKAD) programme, screening and prevention training for supervisors as well as cross-agency cooperation.
Ruslin said AADK had previously conducted drug abuse detection operations involving flight crew, including at MAS in April 2025 and AirAsia in December 2025.
“AADK will continue to work with the police, Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) and international regulatory bodies to strengthen information sharing and security controls at all the country’s main entry points,” he said.
While acknowledging that isolated actions by individuals should not tarnish the image and professionalism of the majority of the country’s dedicated aviation workforce, Ruslin reaffirmed AADK’s commitment to support government and private sector efforts to ensure Malaysia remains free from the threat of drugs.
Meanwhile, he said the implementation of the KAM and SAM programmes at Felda Tenang demonstrated that rural development should not only focus on physical infrastructure, but also include efforts to build human capital that is safe, prosperous and free from drugs.
He said the facilities which were upgraded included the football field pavilion, futsal and sepak takraw courts, Dewan Nurul Ehsan, solar lighting at the cemetery, as well as school learning facilities such as covered walkways, air-conditioning and public address systems.
He said the number of drug addicts and drug abusers in Terengganu fell 7.2 per cent to 7,582 people in the first quarter of 2026 from 8,174 during the same period last year.
“However, the 16.7 per cent increase in involvement among children aged 10 to 14, as well as rising number of cases among those aged 55 to 59 and 65 to 69, is quite worrying,” he said.
He said young people need to be given special attention, with SAM serving as one of the early lines of defence against drug abuse at the school and community levels.
Rusliln said Amphetamine-Type Stimulants (ATS), such as syabu (methamphetamine), yaba pills and ecstasy, remained the most prevalent, accounting for 6,206 cases or 81.9 per cent, followed by opiates with 1,281 cases or 16.9 per cent in the first quarter of this year.
He also called on AADK, Felda, educators, Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), youth and the local community to strengthen cooperation to ensure Felda Tenang and Besut continue to develop with quality infrastructure and remain free from the threat of drugs. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji recovery plan addressed RM12.6b losses but further reforms needed, says RCI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) restructuring and recovery plan successfully restored the institution’s financial position after addressing RM12.6 billion in investment losses, while further reforms are needed to ensure its long-term sustainability, according to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI).
The fully declassified report said RM10 billion of the losses was addressed under the 2018 Recovery Plan, while the remaining RM2.6 billion was resolved progressively through the end of 2025.
It also noted that 75 per cent of its recommendations had been implemented, with the government committed to expediting the remaining 25 per cent as part of ongoing efforts to strengthen governance, investment discipline and risk management.
The effectiveness of the recovery measures was reflected in TH’s improved financial performance, with investment income reaching RM4.64 billion last year, its highest since 2018.
The commission nevertheless stressed that despite the progress achieved, several structural issues must still be addressed to safeguard TH’s long-term sustainability.
A key component of the recovery plan was the transfer of TH’s underperforming assets to Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB), a government-owned special purpose vehicle (SPV), enabling the institution to refocus on its core mandate, particularly the management of haj operations.
The assets were transferred at RM19.9 billion, compared with their market value of RM9.7 billion at the time, representing a premium of RM10.2 billion.
The commission concluded that the transfer preserved TH’s financial position and described the restructuring and recovery plan as instrumental in resolving the institution’s financial crisis.
However, it cautioned that the plan should not be regarded as a long-term solution, identifying several critical issues that remain unresolved.
These include strengthening corporate governance, reviewing the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535), enhancing risk management and cost controls, and introducing a regulatory framework to ensure TH remains resilient.
Among the commission’s principal concerns was the government’s ability to redeem UJSB sukuk and continue providing the annual cash allocations previously promised by the Cabinet.
It warned that failure to do so could result in continued profit distributions to depositors without adequate cash backing.
Separately, TH had previously explained that the transfer of its underperforming assets to UJSB was financed through two sukuk issuances backed by government letters of support, carrying annual profit rates of 4.05 per cent and 4.10 per cent.
The institution also said UJSB had made several offers over the years to sell assets back to TH, although none met the institution’s investment criteria at the time.
Following a fresh review this year, however, TH repurchased land at Tun Razak Exchange (TRX) for RM270 million, compared with the original transfer price of RM400 million.
TH also repurchased the UJ Estates (Holdings) Sdn Bhd oil palm plantation for RM695 million, below its original transfer price of RM800 million.
The institution’s recovery has also been reflected in its annual profit distribution, which rose from 1.25 per cent in 2018 to 3.25 per cent in 2024 and 3.5 per cent in 2025.
TH said the distributions were declared after taking into account RM2.6 billion in impaired assets that could not be transferred to UJSB at the end of 2018 for specific reasons.
It added that its financial position was now significantly stronger and that it had begun rebuilding reserves to support its long-term financial sustainability.
The RCI concluded that while the restructuring and recovery plan had successfully stabilised TH’s financial position, sustained reforms in governance, regulation and risk management remain essential to safeguard the institution’s future resilience. — Bernama

Title: Anwar pledges thorough probe into every Tabung Haji RCI finding following King’s decree
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The government has pledged to investigate every recommendation thoroughly and the findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following a decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
In a Facebook post today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move was in line with the Madani government’s commitment to ensuring a comprehensive investigation into the report.
“I humbly thank His Majesty for granting me an audience to brief him on several important developments concerning the country’s interests and the wellbeing of the people.
“His Majesty’s order for a thorough investigation into the RCI report reflects the Madani government’s commitment to ensuring that every recommendation and finding is fully investigated without compromise,” he said.
Anwar said the matter was among several key developments discussed during his more than hour-long audience with Sultan Ibrahim at Istana Bukit Tunku here today.
He said TH manages a trust built from the hard-earned savings of millions of Malaysians, including farmers, civil servants and middle- and lower-income earners who have spent years saving to perform the haj pilgrimage.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said there could be no betrayal of such a significant trust, and those found to have misused it must be held accountable under the law.
The RCI report on TH, published on July 29, detailed various findings concerning weaknesses in the institution’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
The Prime Minister also briefed the King on developments in the investigation into Federal Land Development Authority (FELDA), saying the government was reviewing the special task force report to determine the appropriate action in accordance with the law.
Anwar said the Madani government remained steadfast in upholding good governance, transparency and accountability, with no one who betrayed the people’s trust spared from firm action, regardless of position or rank.
He said the government would continue to reinforce security controls at the country’s entry points through effective enforcement, continuous surveillance and close inter-agency cooperation to tackle cross-border crime while protecting national security and sovereignty.
“Insya-Allah, I and the entire government will remain committed to His Majesty’s decree to strengthen governance, enforcement and national security, while ensuring the wellbeing of the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MACC, police and IRB ramp up investigations into alleged Tabung Haji irregularities after RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Enforcement agencies have stepped up action following the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), with investigations now focusing on individuals linked to alleged management irregularities at the institution.
By yesterday, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had remanded five individuals to assist in investigations into various alleged misconduct uncovered in the 211-page report released on July 29.
Those remanded for between three and five days comprised individuals from various professional backgrounds, including a former plantation manager, a design company director, a deputy general manager for construction, an occupational safety and health manager, and a project director of a statutory body’s property company.
Separately, the MACC Special Task Force detained the former chief executive officer (CEO) and former chief financial officer (CFO) of a statutory body on Aug 4 to facilitate investigations into alleged abuse of power involving a RM370 million share acquisition involving two plantation companies.
However, both suspects, aged 68 and 60, were released due to health reasons. The former CFO completed giving his statement yesterday, while the former CEO remains on medical leave.
Meanwhile, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), through its Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID), has opened five investigation papers following nine reports lodged by TH, its subsidiaries and members of the public.
CCID director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said investigators were in the process of recording statements from witnesses in Malaysia and abroad, as well as obtaining relevant documents to complete the investigations.
The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) has also begun investigating several individuals after detecting significant discrepancies between their ownership of luxury assets and their declared income.
It said its tax risk analysis had uncovered inconsistencies in the individuals’ income declarations, prompting raids at several premises to seize documents and verify facts relevant to the investigations.
The RCI report, which examined TH’s operations between 2014 and 2020, highlighted numerous governance weaknesses and alleged excessive political interference in profit distribution and haj operations.
Among the report’s most striking findings was that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion for the 2017 financial year, but instead reported an extraordinary profit of RM3.4 billion in its financial statements.
Following severe asset impairment, the report recommended forensic audits into several high-risk investment decisions involving PT TH Indo Plantations, Emrail Sdn Bhd, Wellspring Worldwide Limited, Abraj Sdn Bhd, Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, TH Plantations Bhd, TH Properties Sdn Bhd, Alam Maritim Resources/TH Marine, TH Hotel & Residences Sdn Bhd and FGV Bhd, which allegedly resulted in substantial losses to depositors’ funds.
It also proposed several measures, including recovering RM2.19 million in bonuses paid to TH Properties’ board members and management after finding that the payments did not comply with established regulations.
The report further described bonus payments equivalent to between two and 13 months’ salary awarded to TH staff between 2010 and 2017 as excessive and unjustifiable given the institution’s financial position during that period.
The findings and recommendations are expected to come under scrutiny during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting scheduled for Aug 11 to debate the RCI report.
On Aug 5, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said between 35 and 40 MPs had expressed interest in participating in the special sitting. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s interfaith approach offers lessons for peace, social harmony, says Aaron
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 8 — Malaysia’s experience in managing religious, cultural and ethnic diversity can offer valuable lessons to the international community in advancing interfaith understanding, peace and social harmony, Minister of National Unity Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said.
He said Malaysia’s approach was anchored in the recognition that diversity should not be viewed as a source of division, but as a strength that could be harnessed through mutual respect, openness and cooperation.
Speaking at the International Interfaith Peace Conference (IIPC) 2026 here today, Aaron said interfaith dialogue had an important role in strengthening mutual understanding and building a more cohesive society.
The conference, themed ‘Melaka and Malaysia as a Meeting Point of Faith, Culture, Diversity and Harmony Towards Cohesive Nation Building’, provided an important platform for religious leaders, policymakers and civil society representatives from different parts of the world to exchange ideas and strengthen cooperation in the pursuit of peace and social harmony.
The conference was opened by Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Dr Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam. Also present were founding board member of the Doha International Centre for Interfaith Dialogue (DICID) Prof Dr Hamed Abdulaziz Al-Marwani, special representative of the Foreign Minister on Peace Building and Countering Islamophobia and founding director of Bait Al Amanah Datuk Dr Abdul Razak Ahmad and director of Muslim World League, Malaysia Dr Muhammad Gharawi.
Aaron added that interfaith dialogue should not be misunderstood as an attempt to blur theological differences or create religious uniformity, but rather as a means of promoting accurate understanding among communities of different faiths.
“Interfaith dialogue is not about changing anyone’s faith. It is not about compromising religious principles. Instead, interfaith dialogue is about creating mutual understanding while respecting our differences,” he said.
He said the objective of interfaith dialogue was not to seek theological agreement or produce final binding decisions, but to provide a platform for disseminating accurate information, sharing knowledge and exchanging best practices.
“By disseminating accurate information, interfaith dialogue helps to dispel misconceptions, reduce prejudice and strengthen mutual respect among people of different faiths,” he said.
Aaron said such engagements were also important in empowering young people to become bridge-builders across communities, encouraging collaboration between religious leaders and the government, and reinforcing their shared responsibility in advancing nation-building.
He said the importance of interfaith dialogue had become even more apparent following his participation in several recent engagements, including the Harmony Symposium, World Religious Leaders Conference and Roundtable Discussion on Multi-Faith Partnerships in Praxis for Human Flourishing and Dignity.
Despite differences in themes and participants, he said the engagements shared a common objective of bringing people together through dialogue and deepening mutual understanding through the sharing of interfaith information.
“This is precisely why interfaith dialogue remains as relevant today as ever,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Two killed in separate Perak accidents involving lorry, three vehicles and family car
Article:
IPOH, Aug 8 — Two people were killed in separate accidents, one near the West Coast Expressway (WCE) toll plaza near Teluk Intan and the other at Kampung Pulau Juar near Kampung Gajah.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the Teluk Intan accident today involved a 25-tonne empty lorry and two vehicles, a Toyota Vellfire and a Honda HRV.
He said that in the 6.30 am incident, there were two women, aged 54 and 59, in the Toyota Vellfire.
“The 59-year-old driver, who sustained serious injuries, was rescued by members of the public, but the 54-year-old was trapped in the front passenger seat and was confirmed dead by Ministry of Health (MOH) personnel.
“A 50-year-old man in the Honda HRV suffered minor injuries, while the 31-year-old lorry driver escaped unhurt,” he said in a statement today.
Sabarodzi said the remains of the 54-year-old woman were handed over to the police, while the injured victims received initial treatment from MOH personnel before being taken to hospital by ambulance.
Meanwhile, in the Kampung Gajah incident, Sabarodzi said a Proton Wira, with six family members - a man, a woman, three boys and a girl - on board, skidded into a drain at about 10.50 pm yesterday.
He said the woman and four children were safely removed from the vehicle by members of the public before firefighters arrived at about 11 pm.
“The man, who drove the car, was found unconscious. He was extricated by firefighters and handed over to Health Ministry personnel for treatment and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) at the scene.
“However, Mohd Khirzee Musa, 39, was pronounced dead,” he said, adding that his remains were handed over to police. — Bernama

Title: IRB urged to probe possible tax evasion involving Tabung Haji group, subsidiaries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) should look into possible tax evasion involving the Tabung Haji group and its subsidiaries as investigations intensify following the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) for the 2014-2020 period.
The advisor to the Enforcement Focus Group at the Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission (EAIC) Prof Datuk Mazlan Ahmad said a comprehensive investigation should also be supported by forensic accounting to trace the flow of funds, including their origin, destination and beneficiaries.
“I believe certainly whether the group or the subsidiary commercial sector, they are doing some tax evasion. Therefore, IRB must look into this,” he said in an interview on The Nation programme aired by
Bernama TV.
Mazlan also called for a thorough examination of possible money laundering, noting that tracing suspicious transactions would assist enforcement authorities in identifying the parties involved and determining if criminal offences were committed.
He stressed that the investigation should not be limited to individuals at the management or board level but must scrutinise the entire ecosystem surrounding the institution and its transactions.
“The issue now, very importantly, is to make sure we have the best forensic accounting to really follow the money...where it comes from, where it goes and who benefited from all these schemes. I would say, to sum up, it looks like systemic risk. It is not a one-man show,” he said.
Mazlan noted that the RCI report findings should serve as a springboard for deeper investigation rather than the end of the process, stressing that enforcement agencies must now determine if surface issues point to specific criminal acts and identify those responsible.
He added one of the fundamental problems highlighted by the RCI was a lack of governance, particularly at board level.
As a chartered accountant and council member of the Malaysian Institute of Accountants (MIA), he said the board of directors had a fiduciary duty to provide proper oversight, checks and balances and direction for the organisation.
“The board of directors is accountable for whatever is done by the management. They must perform their fiduciary duty and provide checks and balances,” he said.
The RCI report, which was published on July 29, revealed various important findings related to the management and governance of the institution for the period 2014 to 2020.
A special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat will be held on August 11 to debate the report. — Bernama

Title: Gobind urges fail‑safe layers, says unchecked AI could jeopardise trust and national security
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 8 — Safety and security assessments must precede the adoption and deployment of new technologies to prevent operational failures and safeguard user reliance, said Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo.
While rapid technological advancements, ranging from robotics to Large Language Models (LLMs), offer significant opportunities, users and policymakers must understand the inherent risks, verification processes and control mechanisms required before full implementation.
Speaking at the MyMahir Artificial Intelligence (AI) Roadshow here today, Gobind highlighted a previous high-profile AI event launch that encountered technical glitches involving an autonomous robot, which provided crucial lessons on technological readiness and security controls.
“Actually, we must ensure that it (AI) is safe before we use it. So, we should be in a position where we are sure or certain that it is secure to use the technology before we introduce it and ask people to adopt it class-wide.
“Ultimately, there must also be layers to ensure that if anything goes wrong, we are still in a position to control it,” he added.
Gobind noted that robust digital infrastructure and fail-safe layers are essential in robotics and autonomous deployment.
Addressing the surge in AI adoption, including tools such as ChatGPT and Gemini, Gobind cautioned users to verify the authenticity and accuracy of information before making critical decisions.
On workforce development and national readiness, the minister said Malaysia must proactively upskill its human capital to meet emerging technological needs rather than wait for disruptions to occur.
“So, we need to anticipate what kind of impact technologies will have on jobs, for example, and we have to start taking steps now to make sure that we have people who are ready for that when we get there.
“Because we cannot have a situation where technology arrives, it’s ready for us to use, but we have no talent or understanding to use it to our advantage,” he said.
With the rapid pace of advancement of global technology, remaining static is not an option as competitors and neighbouring nations continue to integrate digital tools across various sectors, including medical, agriculture, transport and security, he said.
“We don’t really have a choice. We have to make sure that we understand what is happening around us. We have to make sure that we are able to use it, because our neighbours are going to use it. In business, our competitors will be using technology. If we don’t, they move far ahead,” he said.
He commended initiatives by Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp) and cross-ministry collaborations aimed at preparing the nation’s workforce for the shifting demands of the future economy.
Over 400 Malaysians gathered today for the 16th and largest edition of the MyMahir AI Roadshow, reflecting growing public demand for practical AI skills and reaffirming the government’s commitment to ensuring Malaysians are prepared for the future of work. — Bernama

Title: Pulau Redang must be protected, Terengganu mulls heavier penalties for violating boat operators
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 8 — The state government will hold an engagement session with tourism operators and relevant agencies to discuss the issue of coral reef damage believed to have been caused by anchoring activities in prohibited areas.
Terengganu Tourism, Culture, Environment and Climate Change Committee chairman Datuk Razali Idris said the meeting, scheduled to be held from August 26 to 28, aims to identify the actual cause of the problem and examine weaknesses in enforcement.
He said the session would not just be a space for discussion, but also serve as a platform for the implementation of stricter action against any parties found violating laws and regulations.
“I take seriously reports of coral reef damage, especially those involving day-trip boats. If the allegations are proven true, such actions are irresponsible and cannot be tolerated.
“The conservation efforts undertaken by the government, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and communities, which have taken decades or even hundreds of years, should not be destroyed in the pursuit of profit,” he said when contacted today.
Razali said the state government would also study proposals to review permits for day-trip operations or impose heavier penalties on boat operators who flout the rules.
He said the state government would not compromise with any day-trip operators or boat operators found to have ignored the stipulated operating procedures, resulting in damage to coral reefs.
“Pulau Redang is a state treasure and a tourism asset that must be protected. All parties must shoulder the responsibility of ensuring environmental sustainability on Pulau Redang rather than just pursuing profits,” he added. — Bernama

Title: DOE confirms haze movement, unhealthy API hits Serian, Kuching, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Bintulu
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 8 — Air quality in the country has worsened, with five areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the five areas with unhealthy API are Serian (171), Kuching (154), Samarahan (154), Sri Aman (139) and Bintulu (124).
She also said that three areas recorded good air quality while 60 areas recorded moderate readings.
“Air quality in the country today has deteriorated, with an increase in the number of areas recording unhealthy API readings, especially in Sarawak, due to haze movement from various directions,” she said in a statement.
She said the Regional Haze Map issued by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) yesterday showed that dry weather conditions would continue over most parts of the southern Asean region today, except for isolated showers over northern Sumatra and Peninsular Malaysia, as detected through imagery from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)-20 satellite.
According to her, the report from ASMC, which is based in Singapore, showed that 643 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 17 in Sumatra and 25 in Malaysia (22 in Sarawak, two in Selangor and one in Terengganu).
“Hotspots were detected extensively in West Kalimantan, while isolated to scattered hotspots were detected in other areas in Kalimantan.
“Several hotspots were also detected, especially in several areas of Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, southern and central Sumatra, as well as eastern Java,” she said.
She said moderate to thick smoke plumes were observed in West Kalimantan and moving northwards into western Sarawak.
Moderate to dense smoke plumes were also observed in other parts of Kalimantan and central Sarawak, while light to moderate smoke plumes were observed over southern and central Sumatra and eastern Java.
Azuri Azizah said the DOE has stepped up enforcement efforts and daily patrols in areas at risk of open burning, in addition to monitoring API readings from time to time.
She said the National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan have been activated to coordinate government agencies’ efforts in addressing open burning and dealing with haze situations in the country.
“The DOE, through the National Haze Action Plan, continuously monitors air quality and the measures to be taken are in line with the action plan involving all relevant agencies,” she said.
Azuri Azizah said that based on the National Haze Action Plan, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) would activate the Disaster Management Committee at the district, level or central level when API readings exceed 150 for more than 24 hours.
Under the action plan, she said all outdoor activities would have to be suspended when API readings exceed 100, while schools, kindergartens and nurseries would have to be closed immediately when readings exceed 200.
“Cloud seeding operations will be carried out, subject to the presence of suitable clouds and appropriate weather conditions, when API readings exceed 150 for more than 24 hours,” she said.
She said the public could obtain the latest hourly API readings through via the DOE’s website at https://eqms.doe.gov.my/APIMS/main or the official MyJAS EQMS application on Google Play and the App Store.
Azuri Azizah also reminded the public not to carry out open burningh or allow their land and premises to be encroached upon, resulting in open burning being carried out intentionally or unintentionally.
“According to the Environmental Quality (Amendment) Act 2024, those found guilty of open burning can be fined a minimum of RM25,000 and up to RM1 million, or imprisoned for up to five years, or both, while a compound of up to 50 per cent of the maximum fine may also be imposed for each offence.
“Members of the public are asked to cooperate in putting out small fires and to report cases of open burning or fires to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DOE’s toll-free line at 1-800-88-2727,” she added. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution vows stronger security, aims to place Malaysia in Global Peace Index top 10
Article:
SANDAKAN, Aug 8 — Malaysia is aiming to achieve a position within the top 10 of the Global Peace Index as Malaysia is currently ranked 12 out of 165 countries.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said within Asean, Malaysia ranked second behind Singapore and third in the Asia-Pacific region below Singapore and New Zealand.
“As we move towards the 13th Malaysia Plan, I have given a specific instruction to my secretary-general that we must work towards achieving a position within the top 10 of Global Peace Index.
“Security and stability create confidence, and confidence becomes the foundation upon which everything else is built,” he said in his speech at a dinner held in conjunction with the security briefing and assessment programme involving foreign representatives to the Eastern Sabah Security Zone (ESSZone) here yesterday.
Saifuddin Nasution also conveyed Malaysia’s appreciation to Australia and the Republic of Korea for their constructive reassessments of travel advisories involving the ESSZone.
“I would also like to express our heartfelt appreciation to Japan for its thoughtful efforts in reviewing and updating its travel advisory on two occasions, reflecting its continued commitment to ensuring that its advice remains aligned with prevailing conditions.
“Most recently, we welcomed the United States’ decision to undertake a similar review,” he added.
Saifuddin Nasution said, a review of these advisories would not only acknowledge Malaysia’s security achievements, but would also strengthen confidence, encourage tourism, promote sustainable investment and further deepen the longstanding friendship between Malaysia and respective countries.
He said, over the last 13 years, the government have invested RM723 million on the security of ESS Zone.
“As a result, we are now in a much better position, the ability to travel freely across our waters, visit our islands and engage with our communities is made possible through the unwavering commitment of the government led by the ministry through Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCOM),” he said. — Bernama

Title: King orders tighter airport security, urges ministries to curb drug smuggling nationwide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia today called on the relevant ministries and agencies to tighten security controls and enhance security measures at all country’s airports and entry points.
In a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page, His Majesty said the measures were important to curb drug smuggling and prevent cross-border criminal activities that could threaten public safety and order.
“Security at the country’s entry points must always be strengthened through more effective enforcement, continuous monitoring and close cooperation among all relevant agencies,” he said.
Earlier, the King granted an audience to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at Istana Bukit Tunku here. — Bernama

Title: King orders thorough probe into Tabung Haji RCI report, says guilty parties must face action
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia today decreed that the investigation into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on the Tabung Haji (TH) Board be carried out exhaustively.
In a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s official Facebook, His Majesty said that the move is important to ensure that all parties responsible are appropriately dealt with, as well as to ensure that the same thing does not happen again in the future.
In addition, Sultan Ibrahim also said that the investigation into the matter should be carried out comprehensively, without compromising on any party found guilty.
“No one should escape action if they are truly found guilty. Most importantly, things like this must not happen again,” said His Majesty.
Earlier, the King granted an audience to Prime Minister Seri Anwar Ibrahim for a meeting that lasted more than an hour at Istana Bukit Tunku, today.
In the meeting, His Majesty was briefed on the contents of the TH RCI Report, as well as current issues involving the Federal Land Development Authority (FELDA).
The RCI report, which was published on July 29, revealed various important findings related to the management and governance of the institution for the period 2014 to 2020.
A special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat will be held on August 11 to debate the report. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Constituency allocations at PM’s discretion, funds should go directly to people
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The special constituency allocation is at the discretion of the Prime Minister, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today, amid controversy over several PKR MPs losing access to the MyKhas portal.
Fahmi said the allocation was not a personal entitlement of MPs and that the Prime Minister had the prerogative to determine how the funds were channelled for the benefit of constituents.
“The special allocation is the Prime Minister’s allocation, so it’s up to him how to channel it.
“What’s important is that the money goes straight to the people and not the MP,” he said.
He was responding to questions about claims of a double standard after several PKR MPs, including Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail, Subang MP Wong Chen and Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung, reportedly lost access to the MyKhas portal, which manages constituency development allocations.
The affected MPs had questioned the abrupt suspension of their access, while party leadership has defended the move as a consequence of political choices following their alignment with alternative political platforms.
Fahmi said there was an existing mechanism for assistance to be channelled to constituents through the Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU) when necessary.
“For those who need help, MyKhas is managed by the ICU. So if there is a need, it can be provided through the ICU.”
He said the mechanism announced by Anwar would see allocations for MPs managed through the Prime Minister’s political office.
Fahmi stressed that the purpose of the allocation was ultimately to ensure assistance reached people in the constituencies.
“So as announced by the PM, the mechanism is managed by the Prime Minister’s Office, so there is no issue arising from this,” said Fahmi.
“The money will then go directly to the people,” he added.
He was speaking to reporters after officiating the Internet Selamat forum with parent-teacher associations (PIBG) at Imbi Hall in Cheras today.

Title: Fahmi: AI cannot replace human moderators in detecting cyberbullying, Tamil language a case in point
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Artificial intelligence (AI) cannot be left entirely in charge of moderating online content as it may fail to understand the nuances of certain languages, particularly when dealing with cyberbullying, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said this was particularly evident in cases involving cyberbullying within the Tamil-speaking community, where AI-based moderation could fail to properly identify harmful or abusive content.
“I’ve noticed cyberbullying among the Indian community is really bad.
“I have told TikTok that the language issue cannot be handed over to AI. It is unable to fully understand the nuances of certain sentences, especially those that harm and bully others.
“TikTok has taken a different approach. They have reduced the number of human moderators and are now more focused on using AI. I will give them some time.”
Fahmi said the government had introduced the Child Protection Code (CPC) and Risk Mitigation Code (RMC), which had been communicated to social media platform operators.
He said the two codes were intended to ensure social media platforms did not become hubs for crimes including scams, cyberbullying and other offences.
“When the platform tries to use AI to do moderation, if they do not have the ability to understand what is happening in a certain language, it will make cyberbullying a huge crime,” he said.
Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) was currently engaging social media platforms, including YouTube, in Singapore over the implementation of the CPC and RMC.
He said platforms had been given several months to study and implement the codes, while discussions were ongoing over their operation.
He added that age verification through electronic Know Your Customer (e-KYC) mechanisms was also being implemented by social media platforms, with platforms that failed to comply once the CPC and RMC were fully implemented facing heavy penalties.
Fahmi was speaking to reporters after officiating the Internet Selamat forum with parent-teacher associations (PIBG) at Imbi Hall in Cheras today.
He said parents also had an important role in protecting children online, including understanding current cyberbullying and scam tactics, being aware of the risks posed by AI and activating parental controls.
He also reiterated the government’s position that children below 16 should not independently open social media accounts, although parents could create accounts for educational purposes.
In 2024, cyberbullying victim Rajeswary Appahu, known as Esha, an influencer, died on July 5, shortly after filing a police report regarding threats and defamation directed at her on social media platforms.

Title: Nurul Izzah remains party member, Anwar has full backing of govt parties, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The resignation of Nurul Izzah Anwar from her party leadership post will not affect her commitment to PKR, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
Fahmi said Nurul Izzah remained a party member and would continue to support its struggle, while stressing that component parties remained committed to supporting Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“Puan Nur Izzah remains as a member of the party and will continue to support the party in the struggle.
“The focus of Parliament and the commitment of the MPs in Parliament is that they will continue to support Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim until the end.”
He said Nurul Izzah had resigned and requested time to focus on her PhD studies, with the party’s leadership responsibilities to continue under its existing leadership structure.
Fahmi said the resignation should not be interpreted as an indication that the government was losing support, stressing that political parties did not automatically leave the government following such developments.
“We are not like the other parties that have said that the parties have automatically left the government. That is not the case. We are not like that.
“In a democracy, we sit down, we discuss. The higher objective is to solve the problems of the people, the economy, and make sure the economy of the people becomes the focus.”
He said the government remained focused on reforms and resolving outstanding issues, including matters arising from the Tabung Haji-related Royal Commission of Inquiry report.
Fahmi said 75 per cent of the recommendations in the report had been implemented, although several issues remained to be addressed.
“The government will continue to implement many reforms that need to be carried out,” he said.
Asked whether recent developments could affect the government, Fahmi said the public should not underestimate the situation, while expressing confidence that Anwar would make further announcements benefiting the people.
“I believe that in the near future, the Prime Minister will make some good announcements for the people and the government,” he said.
On the next general election, Fahmi said it could be held towards the end of next year, while declining to comment further on speculation surrounding its timing.
He was speaking to reporters after officiating the Internet Selamat forum with parent-teacher associations (PIBG) at Imbi Hall in Cheras today.
Nurul Izzah announced that she was relinquishing her role as PKR deputy president to focus on further studies and community work outside politics. Instead of a full resignation, the PKR Central Leadership Council granted her temporary leave starting after the upcoming National Congress, with Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail stepping in to handle her duties.

Title: Police corporal killed in Sabah electrocution laid to rest as family recalls final video call
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 8 — Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, who was believed to have died from an electric shock in Beaufort, Sabah yesterday, was laid to rest at the Kampung Pangkal Kuang Muslim Cemetery in Ketereh here this morning.
The remains of the 29-year-old were laid to rest after funeral prayers were held at his family home in Kampung Hutan Pasir here.
His eldest sister, 34-year-old Nurlella Rahim, said her family expressed their appreciation to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) for assisting in facilitating the arrangements to bring her brother’s remains home.
“The vehicle carrying my brother remains arrived at 4.45 am. I would like to thank PDRM for helping and making the arrangements to bring his remains home,” she told reporters at the cemetery.
Nurlella said the five siblings were very close and often made video calls almost every day, including through the family WhatsApp group.
“We made video calls with each other almost every day. Although I live in Ipoh, Perak, and my brother was in Sabah, we stayed in touch through video calls and social media,” she added.
She said they also regularly commented on one another’s photos posted on social media and often made group video calls through the family WhatsApp group whenever they had free time, and that her late brother’s last video call with their mother was on Thursday afternoon.
“During the video call with our mother, he was tired and was less responsive but still managed to smile. He told her it was okay and that they would continue talking later because he had to report for work.
“Even during short breaks, he would make video calls with us,” she added.
Nurlella said her last video call with her brother was on Sunday, when he took his wife, Fatimah Shahira, and their child to the beach.
In the incident at 5.50 pm, Mohamad Nur Hafiz and two other personnel stationed at the Weston Police Station in Beaufort were confirmed dead after they were believed to have been electrocuted while moving a 29-foot-long metal pole used to hook coconuts outside the station near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Weston.
The other two victims were Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, 40, from Sarawak, and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26, from Terengganu.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered a thorough, transparent and immediate investigation into the incident.
Anwar was quoted as saying in a Facebook post that the investigation was important to determine the cause of the tragic incident and ensure improvements could be made to prevent a similar incident from recurring. — Bernama

Title: Police neutralise unattended luggage at Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS complex, no explosives found
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 8 — Police carried out a process to neutralise a piece of luggage suspected of containing explosives after it was left unattended at Block B of the Immigration/Customs inspection area at the Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex in Bukit Kayu Hitam last night.
Kubang Pasu police chief Supt Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the pink luggage was found at about 5.55 pm after no one came forward to claim it.
“The luggage was then taken for scanning and Customs personnel found images indicating the possible presence of suspected drugs and explosive materials.
“The Bomb Disposal Unit (UPB) from the Kedah Police Headquarters arrived at the scene at 8.45 pm to neutralise the luggage after assessing the risks surrounding the building, with priority given to the safety of lives,” he said.
He said the ICQS Complex was also closed from 9.30 pm to 11.30 pm to facilitate the neutralisation process by the UPB.
“The luggage was opened at 11 pm, and no explosive materials were found. Further inspection found only clothes, oil in a container, a black hairdryer, shampoo and lotion,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Police kill two suspects in shootout during Alor Setar kidnap rescue operation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Two suspects, believed to be foreigners, were killed in a shootout with police during an operation to rescue two kidnap victims at a house in Taman Amira, Telaga Bata, Alor Setar, Kedah, last night.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the incident occurred at about 8.40 pm when the suspects fired several shots at the Special Investigation Division (D9) team from the Bukit Aman CID.
“The raiding team returned fire in self-defence until the threat was neutralised. Both suspects were confirmed dead by medical personnel at about 9.30 pm and no identification documents were found on them,” he said in a statement today.
He said the two victims rescued were foreigners — a man in his 70s and a woman in her 30s — who were found blindfolded and handcuffed.
Kumar said police also found a Beretta semi-automatic pistol loaded with five rounds of ammunition, a revolver containing four rounds of ammunition and a long machete near the two suspects.
Following the incident, he said police launched several raids and arrested six individuals, comprising a local man, four foreign men and a foreign woman, aged between their 20s and 40s, in Kedah, Penang and Kuala Lumpur.
“An application to remand all the suspects will be made today under Section 12 of the Kidnapping Act 1961, while the case is being investigated under Section 3(1) of the same Act for kidnapping for ransom,” he said.
Kumar said the case is still under investigation and advised the public not to speculate or make comments that could interfere with the investigation or distort the facts, causing unnecessary public concern.
“A press conference on this incident will be held on Aug 10 (Monday),” he added. — Bernama

Title: Education minister challenges vocational students to use drones to improve school security
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Students of Setapak Vocational College have been challenged to develop innovative ways of using drone technology to enhance security on their school campus.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the students had been given one month to study and identify the best ways to apply the technology before presenting their proposals to her.
“Within a month, I want the students to present to me how drone technology can be used to help improve school security,” she said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Fadhlina issued the challenge during a collaboration programme between the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education and Setapak Vocational College, which was also attended by South Korean Ambassador to Malaysia Yeo Seung-bae.
She said the programme provided a valuable platform for students to explore robotics and drone technology through the sharing of expertise and experience from South Korea.
Recalling her experience watching the students’ demonstrations, Fadhlina said she was proud of their determination in operating the technological equipment despite encountering setbacks.
“Today, I watched our students fly drones, operate robots and engage with technology. Some succeeded, some made mistakes, but they kept trying. That is where real learning takes place,” she said.
Fadhlina said robotics, drone technology and artificial intelligence (AI) were no longer concepts of the future but had already become part of today’s evolving workplace.
She said the education system must therefore keep pace with technological advancements.
“That is why I gave them the challenge. I want them not only to know how to fly drones, but also to start thinking about how the technology they learn can be used to solve real problems around them,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Cambodia strengthen defence ties, cooperation in AI and drone technology
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Malaysia and Cambodia are committed to further strengthening bilateral ties, particularly in defence and security, while contributing to Asean’s collective resilience.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the commitment was expressed during his courtesy call on Cambodian Prime Minister Samdech Thipadei Hun Manet at the Peace Palace in Phnom Penh yesterday.
He said among the key matters discussed was the effort to finalise the Malaysia-Cambodia Defence Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), which will serve as an important framework to expand and strengthen defence collaboration between the two countries.
“Malaysia and Cambodia also shared views on the importance of Asean centrality, dialogue and regional mechanisms in addressing security challenges, including ongoing efforts towards peace and stability along the Cambodia-Thailand border,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
He added that Malaysia also expressed continued support for the Asean Observer Team (AOT) mechanism, as well as peaceful resolutions through dialogue and negotiations.
Mohamed Khaled said both sides also discussed the importance of finalising the Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea as a crucial step to ensure continued peace, stability and a rules-based order.
He said Malaysia and Cambodia are also committed to strengthening defence cooperation in new areas, including jungle warfare training, the defence industry, artificial intelligence (AI) and drone technology.
Mohamed Khaled also held a meeting with Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence General Tea Seiha to exchange views on the increasingly complex regional security landscape.
In a separate post on the meeting, he expressed hope that the ceasefire between Cambodia and Thailand would be maintained.
“Although Malaysia is no longer the Aseab Chair this year, the country’s commitment to supporting peace and stability in the region remains unchanged.
“I also welcome the progress of the Malaysia-Cambodia Defence Cooperation MoU, which is now in its final stage, and hope it can be signed during the Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) in the Philippines soon,” he said.
Mohamed Khaled said he is confident that the strengthened cooperation will further enhance Malaysia-Cambodia relations ahead of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries in 2027.
Prior to his visit to Cambodia, Mohamed Khaled led the Malaysian delegation on an official working visit to Vietnam on Aug 5 and 6, where he paid a courtesy call on its Prime Minister Le Minh Hung and held bilateral talks with Vietnam’s Defence Minister General Phan Van Giang.
Meanwhile, the Defence Ministry (MINDEF) said the two-day official visit to Cambodia, which began yesterday, reflects Malaysia’s commitment to strengthening defence ties with Asean member states in line with the Defence White Paper.
According to MINDEF, Mohamed Khaled’s working visits to Vietnam and Cambodia are part of the implementation of the Third Pillar of the National Defence Strategy, namely Credible Partnerships, while also reinforcing Malaysia’s defence diplomacy at the regional level.
Also accompanying the Malaysian delegation were Chief of the Royal Malaysian Navy Admiral Tan Sri Zulhelmy Ithnain and Deputy Secretary-General (Policy) of the Defence Ministry Datuk Mohd Yani Daud.  — Bernama

Title: Abang Johari urges community leaders to bridge govt, people
Article:
SARIKEI, Aug 8 — Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg has urged community leaders and heads of ethnic groups to continue serving as a bridge between the government and the people to ensure the state’s development policies are well understood.
He said a clear understanding of government policies was essential to prevent misconceptions that could undermine social harmony, investor confidence and the state’s economic growth.
“Community leaders are not only grassroots leaders but also play an important role in communicating government policies so that the people understand the direction of the state’s development,” he said when speaking at a dinner with community leaders and heads of ethnic groups here last night.
Meanwhile, Abang Johari said education remained the cornerstone of human capital development to ensure Sarawak’s younger generation could compete in a global economy driven by technology and innovation.
In this regard, he said the Sarawak government allocates RM260 million annually to finance free tertiary education for eligible Sarawakians, regardless of their background. — Bernama

Title: Selangor to empower local entrepreneurs to compete globally, says Amirudin
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 8 — The Selangor government remains committed to empowering local entrepreneurs to ensure they can grow sustainably and remain competitive in an evolving digital economy.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said empowering entrepreneurs remains a priority for his administration, as micro-entrepreneurs are among the key drivers of the state’s economic growth.
“The state government will continue to strengthen the entrepreneurial ecosystem through a comprehensive approach encompassing digitalisation, access to financing, capacity building and strategic networks.
“This is to ensure more local entrepreneurs can grow sustainably and compete not only at the national level but also internationally,” he said when speaking at the Platform Selangor Awards Night 2026 (MAPS 2026) here last night.
Also present were Selangor Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Najwan Halimi and MBI Foundation head Ahmad Azri Zainal Nor.
Amirudin said this commitment is reflected through the Platform Selangor (PLATS) initiative, which has brought together more than 100,000 registered entrepreneurs across the state in building an inclusive and sustainable entrepreneurial ecosystem.
Meanwhile, Menteri Besar Selangor (Incorporated) (MBI Selangor) group chief executive officer Datuk Saipolyazan M Yusop said MAPS 2026 was organised to recognise the perseverance, resilience and innovative spirit of entrepreneurs.
He said as a strategic investment agency of the Selangor state government, MBI Selangor through MBI Foundation, remains committed to expanding the impact of socio-economic development through various inclusive entrepreneurship programmes and initiatives in its role as the state government’s strategic investment agency.
“With the support of our strategic partners, we will continue to empower local entrepreneurs to become more resilient, innovative and competitive in an increasingly dynamic economic landscape,” he said.
The highlight of the event saw Minah Satay founder Norminah Syafrial receiving the Selangor State Micro-Entrepreneur Main Award, taking home prizes worth RM20,000, comprising RM5,000 in cash and RM15,000 under the Selangor Madani Entrepreneur Fund (DUMS).
A total of 23 recognitions were presented across nine award categories, including five MAPS 2026 Special Awards, each carrying prizes worth RM18,000, comprising RM3,000 in cash and RM15,000 under DUMS. Other awards included the U-PLATS Halal Excellence Award, the U-PLATS Local Authority Digital Excellence Award and the PLATS Biaya Excellent Entrepreneur Award.
MAPS 2026, organised by the MBI Foundation, was held in collaboration with the Selangor State Economic Planning Unit (UPEN), MBI Selangor and local authorities (PBT). — Bernama

Title: IGP hails new promotion system as boost to morale, career progression
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) described the government’s initiative to introduce a new promotion method for members of the security forces and the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) as a significant recognition and morale booster for both services.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the move, which was highly anticipated by PDRM personnel, reflected the government’s concern for those entrusted with the responsibility of safeguarding public safety and order.
He expressed his deepest appreciation to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the government’s attention towards the agenda of strengthening the career advancement of national security forces personnel.
“PDRM believes that any improvement to the career progression pathway will have a positive impact on the motivation and professionalism of officers and personnel in carrying out their duties,” he said in a statement here last night.
The Prime Minister when addressing the Semarak Kenegaraan programme with MAF personnel at Terendak Camp here today, said the government had, in principle, agreed to reduce bureaucratic hurdles and expedite the promotion process for MAF and PDRM personnel, aligning it with the promotion system for the wider public service.
Anwar said details of the new mechanism were expected to be announced during the Ambang Merdeka celebration at Stadium Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur on Aug 30.
Meanwhile, Mohd Khalid said PDRM was awaiting details of the new mechanism and expressed the force’s readiness to provide full cooperation to ensure its smooth implementation.
He said the government’s commitment would further motivate PDRM personnel to strengthen integrity, enhance professionalism and continue providing quality policing services for the safety and well-being of the people and the country. — Bernama

Title: MACC completes fourth, final day of recording former CFO’s statement in Tabung Haji probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 8 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has completed recording the statement of a former chief financial officer (CFO) of a statutory body-owned company,  as part of its probe into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the individual’s statement was taken to obtain evidence regarding allegations of abuse of power in the purchase of shares in two plantation companies valued at approximately RM370 million.
“Today was the fourth and final day of recording his statement. We began at 9 this morning and ended at 6.30 pm,” he said in a statement yesterday
The MACC detained the 60-year-old individual and the company’s former chief executive officer after they came forward to give their statements at its headquarters on Tuesday.
The investigation focuses on alleged abuse of power in the RM370 million purchase of shares in two plantation companies, as raised in the RCI report on Lembaga Tabung Haji. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji to study NGO proposals, says 75pc of RCI recommendations implemented
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will study all views and proposals contained in a memorandum submitted by non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to help the organisation carry out continuous improvements for the benefit of its 9.8 million depositors.
In a statement yesterday, TH said the memorandum submitted by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on TH Himpunan Aman Solidariti reflected the public’s genuine concern in supporting the national haj institution to safeguard the interests of the Muslim community.
“TH also supports the government’s firm action in taking the necessary measures based on the findings of the RCI.
“TH has implemented more than 75 per cent of the RCI’s recommendations and continues to actively carry out the remaining recommendations as part of its overall improvement efforts, enabling TH’s position today to be far stronger than it was in 2018 following eight years of continuous recovery efforts,” the statement said.
Earlier, the Himpunan Gerakan Islam Malaysia (HIKAM) and the Coalition of Islamic NGOs submitted a memorandum containing 10 demands related to the TH RCI report. Among them were calls for immediate, firm and transparent legal action, the recovery of losses, assets and benefits that had been misappropriated, the open and scheduled implementation of the RCI recommendations, and the continuation of governance reforms under the Madani government.
“Any weaknesses in governance, abuse of power, negligence, breach of trust or vested-interest interference that could undermine TH must be addressed firmly, transparently and in accordance with the law.
“At the same time, this issue should not be exploited for political gain in a manner that creates confusion, division and erodes the confidence of the Muslim community in TH,” HIKAM and the Coalition of Islamic NGOs said in a statement.
HIKAM comprises Persatuan Wadah Pencerdasan Umat Malaysia (WADAH), Pertubuhan IKRAM Malaysia (IKRAM), Pertubuhan Lepasan Institusi Pendidikan Malaysia (HALUAN) and Malaysian Islamic Youth Movement (ABIM).
Meanwhile, Daie Madani said in a separate statement today that the memorandum submitted by the NGOs signified support for all efforts to strengthen TH through governance that is founded on integrity, transparency and accountability.
Daie Madani also expressed its support for the TH administration led by its chairman, Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain, to ensure that depositors’ funds are managed with the highest standards of trust and honesty.
According to Daie Madani, such efforts would also help restore public confidence in an institution that has made significant contributions to the Muslim community in Malaysia.
“We call on the TH management to implement the remaining 25 per cent of the recovery recommendations contained in the RCI report, expose those responsible for tarnishing the image of Islam without fear or favour, and ensure that this dark chapter for the Muslim community is never repeated,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Two men arrested over podcast allegedly touching on religious sensitivities, say police
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 8 — Police confirmed the arrest of two local men following a report received regarding a podcast episode that allegedly touched on religious sensitivities.
North Klang District Police Chief ACP Ramsay Embol said his department received the report on August 5 before the arrests of a freelance host and a businessman, aged in their 30s and 60s respectively, were carried out yesterday.
“Police have received a report regarding a video clip of a podcast created by two individuals discussing the issues of secular and liberal ideologies.
“This video clip was uploaded onto social media platforms where the podcast content touches on religious issues involving elements of Race, Religion, and Royalty (3R),” he said in a statement yesterday.
Ramsay added that the police are committed to conducting investigations professionally, transparently, and fairly, while advising the public not to make any speculations or spread information that could compromise the investigation process.
The case is being investigated under Sections 298, 504, and 505(b) of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Political differences must not stand in way of Federal-state cooperation
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 8 — Differences in the political parties governing the Federal and state governments should not stand in the way of friendship and cooperation between them, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said close ties and cooperation were essential to ensure the people continued to benefit from government initiatives.
“Our system of government requires close cooperation. We may have differing views and belong to different political parties, but these differences should not hinder friendship, goodwill and cooperation that directly benefit the people.
“That is why I would like to express my sincere appreciation and gratitude for the warm welcome in Melaka and the close cooperation extended by the Melaka state government and the Melaka Historic City Council (MBMB).
“We hope that our aspiration to create a sustainable landscape in line with the Malaysia Madani concept will be translated into action and produce tangible results in the near future,” he said.
He said this when officiating at the National Landscape Day celebration, themed ‘Landskap Lestari, Malaysia Madani’ (Sustainable Landscape, Malaysia Madani) at the Hang Jebat Stadium in Krubong here last night.
Also present were Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Meanwhile, Anwar said national development planning should take into account places frequented by the public, including the cleanliness of food stalls.
He said the relevant authorities should allocate dedicated funding for such efforts instead of focusing solely on mega projects that largely benefit higher-income groups.
“Yes, we are known for our impressive landmarks, but we must not forget that the majority of Malaysians do not dine at five-star restaurants. In Kuala Lumpur, about 80 per cent of the people eat at hawker stalls, roadside eateries and small restaurants.
“How much attention do we give to beautifying and keeping these places clean? That is why I say development planning will fail if we do not strike the right balance,” he said.
The prime minister said development must be carried out in a balanced manner across all sectors to enhance the country’s standing on the world stage. — Bernama

Title: Stay or go? DAP faces catch-22 as crucial congress vote looms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — DAP delegates will gather on August 16 for the party’s national congress, where they will face a political catch-22 that could shape its strategy heading into the next general election.
Roughly 4,000 delegates are expected to vote on whether DAP leaders should remain in government posts, including the federal Cabinet, or relinquish those positions while continuing to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Parliament.
The decision comes after a difficult 10 months for the party.
DAP lost all eight seats it contested in the Sabah election last November before suffering further setbacks in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
Among the casualties was its secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook, who lost his Chennah state seat in the Jelebu parliamentary constituency after serving three terms.
The Cabinet dilemma
The setbacks have fuelled frustration among grassroots members who believe governing has cost DAP politically without producing enough reforms to justify the compromises made over the past three and a half years.
Delegates are now weighing two competing risks.
Grassroots frustration has grown over what members see as insufficient reform despite DAP’s compromises during more than three years in government. — File picture by Shafwan Zaidon
Remaining in government could reinforce criticism that the party has compromised too much while reforms have progressed too slowly.
Leaving the Cabinet, meanwhile, could satisfy members demanding a stronger stance but create a different political challenge.
Many voters may not distinguish between leaving the executive and continuing to support the government in Parliament.
Instead, a Cabinet exit could be viewed as a sign that the unity government is losing cohesion before the next general election, which must be held by February 2028.
The competing pressures reflect the different audiences DAP is trying to address.
Grassroots members want the party to acknowledge that recent election setbacks were linked to slower-than-expected reforms while in government.
Many voters, meanwhile, may expect parties in government to complete a full parliamentary term, particularly after stability has been repeatedly presented as essential for economic growth and policy reforms.
A precedent in Melaka
DAP leaders have already ruled out withdrawing parliamentary support for Anwar or leaving Pakatan Harapan.
The proposed arrangement of relinquishing executive positions while remaining politically aligned with the government has a recent, though not exact, parallel in Melaka.
Last month, Melaka DAP withdrew from the state government after objecting to a Bill allowing the appointment of nominated assemblymen.
Its representatives resigned from their state administration posts and its four assemblymen moved to the Opposition bench, although the BN-led state government remained intact as BN retained a two-thirds majority in the assembly.
The August 16 vote will determine whether DAP adopts a similar arrangement at the federal level by remaining part of the governing coalition while stepping out of the executive.
No easy answer
International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Associate Professor Syaza Shukri said the debate ultimately centres on whether voters believe the government’s reform agenda has delivered meaningful change.
“The biggest concern is the lack of reform and when we say reform we have to understand it’s about reforms that are felt on the ground.
“Meaning that economic reforms that improve lives and ease of doing business. We’re talking about reforms that would not make Malaysians feel marginalised. Things seem to stay the same,” she said.
Syaza said a vote to remain in government would suggest delegates had chosen the more pragmatic course of helping the administration continue implementing its agenda.
Recent tensions between DAP and Umno surfaced in Negeri Sembilan after Ahmad Zahid Hamidi urged voters to ‘kasi bungkus’ Anthony Loke, highlighting strains between key partners in the unity government. — File picture by Yusof Mat Isa
“But the implication is how can they explain this to the grassroots. Because pragmatism is basically the compromise thus far and we know that’s not very popular.”
She described leaving the Cabinet while maintaining parliamentary support as the clearest middle ground.
“I think this is already the best middle ground, which is leaving the Cabinet but not pulling parliamentary support.
“Pulling parliamentary support would cause the fall of the government. Not doing anything would not solve anything as well,” she said.
Even so, Syaza believes many Malaysians may not appreciate the distinction.
“Average voters may not understand the difference between pulling out of executive versus legislative. So public perception would be that Anwar has lost confidence.”
She said such a perception could weaken Pakatan Harapan heading into the next general election, particularly as Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional appear to have regained political momentum.
Akademi Nusantara senior fellow Azmi Hassan also expects delegates to favour leaving the Cabinet while maintaining support for Anwar.
He said delegates broadly reflect the mood among grassroots members and supporters.
“I think they are more effective as the critical voice of the government. Similar to Umno, they have their Pemuda, which should be very critical of the top leadership. So DAP should be there. I think they are good at that,” he said.
According to Azmi, remaining in government has limited DAP’s ability to champion policies that resonate with its supporters.
“So I think it is best for them to opt out of the government but at the same time support the prime minister so that the stability of the Anwar government remains intact,” he said.
He said the congress provides delegates with an opportunity to reassess the party’s direction after successive election setbacks while keeping Pakatan Harapan intact ahead of GE16.
Leaving the Cabinet could give DAP greater distance from the government, but voters may interpret the move as a sign that Anwar has lost confidence within his coalition. — Bernama file pic
Looking ahead to GE16
Whichever way delegates vote, the political risks remain.
Remaining in government could deepen frustration among members who believe the party needs greater distance from the administration.
Leaving the Cabinet could satisfy those members while inviting questions over the unity government’s cohesion and DAP’s ability to influence policy from outside the executive.
The result is expected to shape DAP’s role in government for the remainder of the parliamentary term, as well as how the party positions itself before Malaysians return to the general polls.

Title: Anwar: Govt to cut red tape in military, police promotion process
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 7 — The government has, in principle, agreed to reduce bureaucratic hurdles and expedite the promotion process for personnel of the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), bringing it in line with the promotion system for the rest of the public service.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said details of the new mechanism are expected to be announced during the Ambang Merdeka celebration at Stadium Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur on August 30.
He said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Public Service director-general Tan Sri Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz are currently finalising the implementation mechanism.
“We will give them a little more time,” he said when addressing the ‘Semarak Kenegaraan’ programme with MAF personnel at Terendak Camp here today.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Dr Mohd Na’im Mokhtar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Shamsul Azri and Army Chief Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.
Anwar said the issue of promotions for MAF officers was raised directly with him during his visit to Syed Sirajuddin Camp in Gemas, Negeri Sembilan, last month. — Bernama
